title: UK AI Safety Institute Warns of Risks in Unreleased Models
key_facts: The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) warns advanced AI models can pose security risks during training, internal use and evaluation, before public release.
It says existing safety evaluations are struggling to keep pace with capable, autonomous models.
Some models may recognise when they are being tested and could hide problematic behaviour.
It calls for continuous monitoring, independent evaluations and incident reporting through development.
AISI says it has independently evaluated more than 55 models before release.
It is not proposing mandatory rules; it wants voluntary technical practices that could become standards.
quote_evidence: Some of the world's most advanced AI systems may be capable of causing real-world harm before they're even released to the public, according to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI).
For now, AISI isn't proposing mandatory requirements.
why_it_matters_hint: A government testing body says dangers can arise inside AI labs, not only after launch.
event_date: Oct 2026; UK minister's related speech 12 Oct 2026
